newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec PPI reassures despite energy price boost.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec PPI reassures despite energy price boost.

text.p: U.S. wholesale prices were relatively well-behaved in December and sent few worrisome inflation signals, despite solid gains in energy prices which could become a concern longer-term, economists said on Thursday.

High energy prices were behind an unexpectedly strong 0.5 percent gain in the December Producer Price Index. But the core numbers, which exclude volatile energy prices and are considered a more reliable gauge of long-term price trends, were reassuringly low.
Overall energy goods gained at a 3.1 percent rate in December, contributing to the biggest overall PPI gain since December of 1995.

But analysts stressed the fact that core products remained encouraging across the board. The headline core rate rose a paltry 0.1 percent in December while intermediate and crude core goods posted 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent gains, respectively.
"The market was looking for a 2.5 percent advance in energy prices as a worst possible scenario," said Anthony Chan, chief economist at Banc One Investment Advisors Corp.
"The underlying tone of the numbers still doesn't suggest any major deterioration, but still energy has to be a concern moving forward," he noted.

Other areas of the December report were roughly in line with expectations, with consumer food prices dropping off 0.1 percent, passenger cars rising 0.3 percent and capital equipment gaining at a 0.1 percent pace.

For 1996 overall, the report showed that PPI rose 2.8 percent after an increase of 2.3 percent in 1995. Excluding food and energy prices, the index posted a meager 0.6 percent rise for the year compared to a 2.6 percent advance in 1995.
Wall Street economists had forecast a 0.3 percent overall rise in December wholesale prices and a 0.1 percent gain in the core.

After dipping initially on the stronger-than-expected headline number, U.S. Treasuries warmed up to the well-behaved core rate, and recovered to trade in solidly positive territory shortly thereafter.
The Labor Department is scheduled to release its report on December consumer prices on Tuesday, January 14.
